Unknown salary stays typed NULL; erasure request

Unverified employer or invalid salary rejected
Search published jobs > inspect questions > select own resume > answer required questions > insert unique application > append applied event
Duplicate apply; closed job; unanswered required question
Shortlist visible candidate > schedule interview > record interview > issue offer > record acceptance and joining > append every status event
Illegal transition; expired offer; withdrawn application
Consultant requests access > employer accepts/declines > recheck consultant openness > submit candidate shortlist > close on job closure
Job closes to consultants before submission
Recruiter selects own-company job > filter blocked candidates > create batch > lock wallet > debit once > recheck consent/block > enqueue delivery
Candidate blocks actor after batching; insufficient credits
Candidate selects party > create user/company block > invalidate visibility cache > exclude search/view/export/outreach > append denied-read evidence
Existing caches and export links must reauthorize
Worker creates separate gig profile > declares service/rate/availability > requester posts gig > worker applies > requester accepts > validate nonoverlap > create handoff
Persist external handoff key > ingest idempotent provider event > reconcile assignment status > snapshot external earnings > requester rates completed gig
Provider down; duplicate or out-of-order completion
Lock licence > allocate available seat > register owned device > lock user > expire stale sessions > count active sessions > admit or deny > audit/revoke
Concurrent final seat; expired session; revoked device
Choose plan > create nonoverlapping period > create payment order > verify provider capture > append payment and credit > issue invoice > bound cumulative refunds
Duplicate capture; overlapping period; excessive refund
Authorize recruiter and candidate visibility > lock wallet > reuse idempotency key or append debit > append download event > issue short-lived object access
Blocked user; retry uses same idempotency key
Update language/privacy/channel preference > match published job alert > check purpose consent > enqueue notification > recheck opt-out > record provider delivery
Consent revoked before delivery; provider unavailable
Create post or support ticket > moderate or assign > append reaction/referral events > resolve/reopen ticket > localize FAQ > record candidate activity
Abusive content; ticket reopen; repeated referral event
Version reference codes/translations > apply role grants > refresh conformed dimensions > load facts at declared grain > aggregate KPIs > record failures
Missing translation falls back; stale dimensions flagged
Receive external or retention trigger > validate version/policy > reconcile or quarantine > unlink expired personal tokens > purge authorized data > append evidence
Provider retries; expired retention; financial token unlink

sections.name: B T193 1. Unified Rules Catalogue v2
rows: Every table uses an integer surrogate key id; foreign keys and check constraints are enforced by the database.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid

Candidates register themselves (or via staff at a placement drive); recruiters/employers cannot register candidates. Sign-up creates user, credential, candidate role, profile, and mandatory terms + privacy consents in one transaction.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid

A candidate profile is visible to recruiters only when deleted_at IS NULL, profile_visibility_id <> 3 (not hidden), and the candidate currently grants profile_visible_to_recruiters consent (purpose 3).
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid

When a candidate blocks an organisation or user, the blocked party immediately loses visibility of the candidate profile, their applications, and their contact details (even if previously downloaded), and never sees the block row.
RLS on candidate_profile, application, candidate_block + candidate_contact()
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid
Permissions derive strictly from user_access_role -> access_role_permission, and only users with account_status_id = 1 (active) hold any permission.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid
Consent is an append-only history per user and purpose with policy_version; the latest record (consent_current) governs processing.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid

Active sessions per user cannot exceed the device limit (3 for candidates; subscription.max_devices_per_user for org members, or 1 without an active subscription). Expired sessions are closed first; revoked devices and over-limit logins are refused and audited.
auth_open_session() with FOR UPDATE lock on app_user + auth_revoke_device()
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid
After 5 consecutive failed password checks, the credential is locked for 15 minutes (locked_until), audited, and refused by auth_open_session(); a successful login resets the counter.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid

An organisation has at most subscription.max_seats current members (valid_to IS NULL) under its active subscription (1 without one). A user belongs to at most one organisation at any point in time, and closed memberships (valid_to) are write-once.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid

Tax identifiers (GSTIN, PAN, CIN, VAT, EIN) are validated for format, tokenised via pii_hmac() + identifier_last4, and never stored in clear. Staff verify or reject organisations via organisation_set_verification(), recording verified_at and an audit event.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid

Publishing a job (draft -> open) sets published_at (write-once) and debits 5 credits from the organisation wallet exactly once (idempotency_key = job_post:<id>). Published jobs never return to draft; closed and filled are final.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid

Each application moving to joined increments job_requirement.positions_filled under a job row lock; when positions_filled = positions_total, job_status_id automatically becomes filled (5); joins beyond positions_total are refused.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid

A candidate can apply at most once per job, only while the job is open (2), not deleted, and on or before closes_on, starting in status applied (1). Attached resumes must belong to the candidate; answers must belong to questions of that job.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid
Applications move only along the 12 edges in application_status_transition; joined, rejected, and withdrawn are final.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid
A candidate may only transition their own application to withdrawn (7); all forward and rejection moves require an unblocked member of the hiring organisation with application_manage permission.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid
Every application status change is recorded in application_status_history (append-only) with from_status_id, to_status_id, changed_at, and created_by.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid

A sold subscription is an immutable licence snapshot (max_seats, max_devices_per_user, starts_on, plan_id cannot change; ends_on cannot be extended; cancelled_at is write-once); subscription periods of one organisation never overlap.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid

Every organisation has exactly one wallet. wallet.balance_credits equals SUM(wallet_ledger_entry.credits) and is never negative. Ledger entries are append-only; corrections are reversal entries (ledger_entry_type_id = 6) pointing once at the original entry.
trg_organisation_ensure_wallet, wallet_post() with wallet row lock, forbid_change(), ck_wallet_balance_not_negative
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid

Payment webhooks (billing_apply_payment_event) are idempotent on gateway_event_ref, verify event.amount = order.amount, advance payment_order strictly forward (created -> authorised -> captured -> refunded or -> failed), issue a sequential GST invoice (18% tax split) on capture, and reverse granted credits on refund.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid

Downloading a candidate profile (billing_download_profile) costs 1 credit and grants the organisation 30 days of access to candidate_contact(). Repeat downloads within 30 days are free and return the existing download. Every download and contact reveal is audited.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid

Notifications are written in the same transaction as the business event (dedupe_key prevents duplicates), honour notification_preference opt-outs and consent_current (except category 3 account_security), never contain PII in payload, and move only queued -> sent -> delivered/failed with exponential backoff up to 5 attempts.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid

Every sensitive action writes an append-only audit_event via audit_log() (actor taken from app.user_id, never forged by the caller); row-change triggers log changed column names, never personal values.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid

Right to erasure (candidate_erase) deletes education, experience, skills, languages, job alerts, resumes (queuing object-storage deletion), and credentials; blanks name, headline, summary, city, salary, email, phone, application_answer.answer_text, and user_device.device_label; ends sessions; revokes devices; and retains applications, downloads, and ledgers anonymised.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid

Organisation parent hierarchy (parent_organisation_id) must remain a strict tree (no self-parenting or cycles), and a recruiter sees and acts only on their own organisation's jobs, applications, and funnel.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid
Consultant-sourced applications (application_source_id = 3) are permitted only on job requirements where is_open_to_consultants = true.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid
All UI strings resolve via ui_text(ui_label_id, language_id) with automatic fallback to English (language_id = 1); user-authored text is stored once in UTF-8 with its language tag.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid

Scheduled retention and maintenance jobs keep high-volume tables bounded: audit_event partitions created monthly and dropped after 7 years; inactive profiles erased after 3 years; ended sessions purged after 1 year; final notifications after 180 days; system errors after 90 days; agg_hiring_funnel_monthly refreshed hourly CONCURRENTLY.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid

Probable duplicate candidates (same phone_e164 and lower(full_name)), profiles missing current_city_id, experience mismatches, over-seat lapsed orgs, unverified org open jobs, and 90-day stale is_open_to_work profiles are continuously detected by data-quality queries (F-01..F-06).
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid

Every table uses an integer surrogate key id; foreign keys and check constraints are enforced by the database.
Every row has positive bigint surrogate id
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation

Candidates register themselves (or via staff at a placement drive); recruiters/employers cannot register candidates. Sign-up creates user, credential, candidate role, profile, and mandatory terms + privacy consents in one transaction.
Recruiter cannot register candidate on behalf
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation

A candidate profile is visible to recruiters only when deleted_at IS NULL, profile_visibility_id <> 3 (not hidden), and the candidate currently grants profile_visible_to_recruiters consent (purpose 3).
Blocked party never receives profile visibility
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation

When a candidate blocks an organisation or user, the blocked party immediately loses visibility of the candidate profile, their applications, and their contact details (even if previously downloaded), and never sees the block row.
Blocked party never receives profile visibility
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation
Permissions derive strictly from user_access_role -> access_role_permission, and only users with account_status_id = 1 (active) hold any permission.
Session device belongs to session user
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation
Consent is an append-only history per user and purpose with policy_version; the latest record (consent_current) governs processing.
Delivery allowed only with purpose consent and channel enabled
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation

Active sessions per user cannot exceed the device limit (3 for candidates; subscription.max_devices_per_user for org members, or 1 without an active subscription). Expired sessions are closed first; revoked devices and over-limit logins are refused and audited.
Reducing limits cannot invalidate active seats or sessions
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation
After 5 consecutive failed password checks, the credential is locked for 15 minutes (locked_until), audited, and refused by auth_open_session(); a successful login resets the counter.
Session device belongs to session user
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation

An organisation has at most subscription.max_seats current members (valid_to IS NULL) under its active subscription (1 without one). A user belongs to at most one organisation at any point in time, and closed memberships (valid_to) are write-once.
Exactly one blocked user or organisation target is present
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation

Tax identifiers (GSTIN, PAN, CIN, VAT, EIN) are validated for format, tokenised via pii_hmac() + identifier_last4, and never stored in clear. Staff verify or reject organisations via organisation_set_verification(), recording verified_at and an audit event.
Raw card, bank and national identifier data is not stored
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation

Publishing a job (draft -> open) sets published_at (write-once) and debits 5 credits from the organisation wallet exactly once (idempotency_key = job_post:<id>). Published jobs never return to draft; closed and filled are final.
Consultant requires open job plus accepted request
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation

Each application moving to joined increments job_requirement.positions_filled under a job row lock; when positions_filled = positions_total, job_status_id automatically becomes filled (5); joins beyond positions_total are refused.
Source version increases monotonically under row lock
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation

A candidate can apply at most once per job, only while the job is open (2), not deleted, and on or before closes_on, starting in status applied (1). Attached resumes must belong to the candidate; answers must belong to questions of that job.
Status/reference value must belong to expected domain
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation
Applications move only along the 12 edges in application_status_transition; joined, rejected, and withdrawn are final.
An answer option must belong to the application question
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation
A candidate may only transition their own application to withdrawn (7); all forward and rejection moves require an unblocked member of the hiring organisation with application_manage permission.
An organisation cannot be its own ancestor
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation
Every application status change is recorded in application_status_history (append-only) with from_status_id, to_status_id, changed_at, and created_by.
Every row has positive bigint surrogate id
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation

A sold subscription is an immutable licence snapshot (max_seats, max_devices_per_user, starts_on, plan_id cannot change; ends_on cannot be extended; cancelled_at is write-once); subscription periods of one organisation never overlap.
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation

Every organisation has exactly one wallet. wallet.balance_credits equals SUM(wallet_ledger_entry.credits) and is never negative. Ledger entries are append-only; corrections are reversal entries (ledger_entry_type_id = 6) pointing once at the original entry.
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation

Payment webhooks (billing_apply_payment_event) are idempotent on gateway_event_ref, verify event.amount = order.amount, advance payment_order strictly forward (created -> authorised -> captured -> refunded or -> failed), issue a sequential GST invoice (18% tax split) on capture, and reverse granted credits on refund.
Refund uses captured payment currency and cannot exceed captured amount
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation

Downloading a candidate profile (billing_download_profile) costs 1 credit and grants the organisation 30 days of access to candidate_contact(). Repeat downloads within 30 days are free and return the existing download. Every download and contact reveal is audited.
Access requires current membership in the requirement organisation
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation

Notifications are written in the same transaction as the business event (dedupe_key prevents duplicates), honour notification_preference opt-outs and consent_current (except category 3 account_security), never contain PII in payload, and move only queued -> sent -> delivered/failed with exponential backoff up to 5 attempts.
Same event key+same digest has one effect; different digest is quarantined
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation

Every sensitive action writes an append-only audit_event via audit_log() (actor taken from app.user_id, never forged by the caller); row-change triggers log changed column names, never personal values.
Every row has positive bigint surrogate id
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation

Right to erasure (candidate_erase) deletes education, experience, skills, languages, job alerts, resumes (queuing object-storage deletion), and credentials; blanks name, headline, summary, city, salary, email, phone, application_answer.answer_text, and user_device.device_label; ends sessions; revokes devices; and retains applications, downloads, and ledgers anonymised.
Session device belongs to session user
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation

Organisation parent hierarchy (parent_organisation_id) must remain a strict tree (no self-parenting or cycles), and a recruiter sees and acts only on their own organisation's jobs, applications, and funnel.
Recruiter acts only on own company requirements
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation
Consultant-sourced applications (application_source_id = 3) are permitted only on job requirements where is_open_to_consultants = true.
Consultant requires open job plus accepted request
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation
All UI strings resolve via ui_text(ui_label_id, language_id) with automatic fallback to English (language_id = 1); user-authored text is stored once in UTF-8 with its language tag.
Resolve requested language then English; never display a raw key
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation

Scheduled retention and maintenance jobs keep high-volume tables bounded: audit_event partitions created monthly and dropped after 7 years; inactive profiles erased after 3 years; ended sessions purged after 1 year; final notifications after 180 days; system errors after 90 days; agg_hiring_funnel_monthly refreshed hourly CONCURRENTLY.
Start <= last activity < expiry; ended sessions are excluded
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation

Probable duplicate candidates (same phone_e164 and lower(full_name)), profiles missing current_city_id, experience mismatches, over-seat lapsed orgs, unverified org open jobs, and 90-day stale is_open_to_work profiles are continuously detected by data-quality queries (F-01..F-06).
No raw national ID, card data or credentials in external bodies or attempt logs
Candidate topical relation; do not join rules by number or inherit implementation

sections.name: B T283 6. Documented Standard Deviations
rows: Reference and configuration tables (language, ui_label, ui_translation, currency, country, state, city, skill, access_role_permission, application_status_transition, job_status_transition, and the 23 lookup tables) omit created_by / updated_by.

Reference and configuration rows are immutable at runtime and versioned exclusively via git migrations (V002, V003, V007, V013); git commit history is their audit trail. Verified by t01_standards.sql L86-89.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid
Rule Group 2 & 4 (Primary Key & Audit Columns on Logs)
audit_event has composite PK (id, occurred_at) and both audit_event and system_error omit created_at/by, updated_at/by.

PostgreSQL declarative partitioning requires the partition key (occurred_at) in the primary key. Log tables record occurred_at and actor_app_user_id / app_user_id natively and are append-only, so updated_at/by would be redundant.
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid

Role-qualified foreign keys (parent_organisation_id, blocked_organisation_id, blocked_app_user_id, sourced_by_app_user_id, actor_app_user_id, from_status_id, to_status_id, renewed_from_subscription_id, reverses_ledger_entry_id) prepend the role to <table>_id.
Disambiguates self-references and tables with multiple foreign keys to the same parent while still ending in _id (verified by t01_standards.sql L44-49).
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid
Foreign keys pointing to static reference/lookup tables and created_by / updated_by audit columns do not carry dedicated B-tree indexes.

Reference/lookup rows and users with history are RESTRICT-protected and never hard-deleted, so PostgreSQL never scans child tables for cascading deletes on those columns, saving ~35% index storage overhead. Every FK to a business table is indexed (t01_standards.sql L53-59).
Source B design/report; not independently executed in hybrid

sections.name: Failure policy
rows: Never trust account ID from body; bind credential to account
Same event key, same payload hash
Manual resolution and separately keyed corrected event
Compare source version under entity lock
Exponential jitter 1s base; 300s cap; max8 attempts; honour bounded Retry-After
At-least-once delivery with idempotent business effect
Malformed/unknown field, invalid enum or FK
Quarantine safe field path and reason
Re-check preference, blocking, consent and expiry before every send
Open after5 failures in30s; probe after30s; proposed limits
Pause producer above budget; preserve committed intents
Version allowlist, compatibility fixture, additive rollout
Source row count or money totals disagree
Source = applied + rejected + duplicates + pending; compare exact decimal by currency
Portable count check; external totals pending

sections.name: Source ownership
rows: payment_event provider reference/status/amount; no card data
verification_record token/outcome; no raw national ID
Keep pending; retry without enabling publication
External system owns fulfilment and earnings
Pending handoff; reconcile stale events by version
Legacy is source until field-level cutover

User-confirmed steps1-22: Discover1-5, Model6-12, Prove13-21, Platform step22. Steps23-28 are outside scope.
Current version
v3.0 prepared2026-10-28. Prior v1/v2 snapshots preserved.
Hierarchy
D5 semantics: L1 section; L2 parameter; L3 value-contract or meaning/lineage facets; L4 atomic type, allowed values, requiredness, definition, reason and source.
Rubric
Eight D5 core dimensions reweighted to90 plus10 step-specific. Weights14,14,9,18,9,9,9,8,10 total100.
Scale
5 >=98%;4 >=90%;3 >=75%;2 >=50%;1 >0%;0 absent or unassessed. Judgment dimensions require written evidence.
Full rating
SUM(weight*score/5). Independent content comparison and human understanding are unassessed and contribute0; no independent review is fabricated.
Observed rating
Full contributions divided by83 observed weight, excluding9 independent consistency and8 human understanding. This is a supplementary view, not the acceptance score.
Acceptance
Accept only full score>=90 and every critical dimension>=4. Rework below75; otherwise Refine. Release gates remain separately open regardless of documentary scores.
Rollup
Step=25% schema+25% scorecard+50% output. Project and phase ratings use P0 weight3/P1 weight2/P2 weight1. These are disclosed project choices.
Section ratings
Average of measured structure, documentary fill, source/definition quality and evidence readiness. L1-L4 ratings describe contract quality, not production capacity.
Peer inputs
Amber0-5 cells are editable; blank peer cells mean not reviewed. Consolidated workbook owns the authoritative editable rating snapshot. Per-step files calculate independently.
Evidence
Baseline v2 suite re-executed1565/1565. V3 portable validation348/348. SQLite/static/Python layers only. Native PostgreSQL, real provider callbacks, concurrency, target volume and recovery NOT RUN.
Capacity
Editable assumptions drive RPS, burst DB concurrency, storage and connection ceilings. No number is a measured deployment capacity.
HTML refresh
The HTML embeds this saved data snapshot. It includes all output records and can search/filter/download them. Regenerate after approved Excel/source changes.
Source priority
User request controls the22-step cap and deliverables. D1 controls business scope. D3 controls lifecycle numbering. D5 controls quality method. D2/D4 guide scenarios and refinement.
Production boundary
120 tables and1250 columns provide the current design. Schema breadth cannot guarantee arbitrary user count or zero production defects. Required release evidence is owned and visible.
Kluster
Requested Kluster tools unavailable in this session. No Kluster verification is claimed.

What data the platform holds, how much, how it is read and written, how long it is kept, where it comes from, and what "good data" means. This document drives the model: every index in [06](06-physical-model.md) exists for an access pattern listed here.
Highest class = the most sensitive column of the entity (docket rule group 6). Volume: rows at dev scale (measured), then full scale (projected, §3).
who downloaded whom, for which debit
35 tables (geography, currencies, languages, skills, UI labels, 25 lookups)
readable by anyone, including guests (open jobs only)
names, email, phone, profile sections, answers, IP addresses
the person; employers only within visibility and blocking; contact details only after a paid download, audited
password hashes, session tokens, device ids, tax identifiers, gateway references
hashed (argon2id, SHA-256) or tokenised (HMAC + last 4); credentials unreadable by every runtime role
The class of each column is in the [data dictionary](data-dictionary.md) (generated from column comments; test t01 fails if an identifying column lacks its class).
**Measured at dev scale** (10k profiles; `pg_total_relation_size`, so heap plus indexes plus update churn):
profile sections (skill, language, education, experience, resume)
identity (user, credential, role, consent, device, session)
**Projected to full scale** (10M profiles, 1M jobs, 100M applications), using the measured bytes per row:
76 GB (about 40 GB right after VACUUM FULL; the dev figure includes pipeline-update churn)
**~235 GB**, within one primary with NVMe; indexes ~40% of it
**Workload at full scale.** Assumption A-06: 10% daily active users (1M), peak hour five times the average.
job and candidate searches (AP-01, AP-04, AP-05)

Conforms to schema [S-10](schemas.md#s-10--data-dictionary-v1). The single source of truth for what each field means: table, column, business name, PostgreSQL type, constraints, business definition, example, class and owner. Class follows docket rule group 6 as currently tagged in the model; the reviewed classes are in [step 12](12-data-classification-register.md).

**Columns on every business table** (not repeated): `created_at` timestamptz NOT NULL (when the row was created), `created_by` bigint FK → app_user (who created it; NULL = a system process), `updated_at` timestamptz NOT NULL, `updated_by` bigint FK → app_user (NULL = system); all set by the `set_audit_columns` trigger, so no caller can fake them.
• Every table has a surrogate `id`. A column `<table>_id` references that table; a role-named key says its role first (`sourced_by_app_user_id`, `blocked_organisation_id`).
• Columns ending in a lookup name (`application_status_id`) reference an enumeration; join its `code` for logic and `ui_text(ui_label_id, <language>)` for display.
• Times are `timestamptz` in UTC; show them in `app_user.time_zone`. Money is always beside its `*_currency_id`.
• Row-level security filters every business table by the signed-in user, so a query returns only what that user may see.
**Worked example**, written only from this dictionary: applicants of job 2044 by stage, labels in Hindi.

SELECT p.full_name, ui_text(s.ui_label_id, 2::smallint) AS stage, a.applied_at
FROM application a
JOIN candidate_profile p ON p.id = a.candidate_profile_id
JOIN application_status s ON s.id = a.application_status_id
WHERE a.job_requirement_id = 2044
ORDER BY s.sort_order, a.applied_at;

• **Right to erasure:** one function, `candidate_erase()`, in one transaction: profile sections, resumes (files through the outbox), credentials and alerts are deleted; name, contact and salary are blanked; applications, downloads, ledgers and consent evidence stay, pointing at an anonymous profile, because other parties have a legal or contractual right to them. Inactive for 3 years → the scheduler runs the same function.
• **Minimisation:** no card or bank data, no raw national or tax identifier, no message bodies, no password; resume files outside the database; audit details hold column names, never values.
• **Contact details are paid and audited:** an employer reaches email and phone only through a download in the last 30 days, and every read writes an audit event.
• **Test data never holds real personal data:** the generator makes names and uses reserved `.test` domains and generated phone numbers; production data is never copied to development.
• **Open findings:** FND-09 (consent purposes not enforced), FND-10 and FND-11 (erasure leaves answer text and device names), FND-12 (reclassification).

job_status_id and published_at were both updatable by v2_app; clearing published_at allowed a published job to return to draft (violating FR-JOB-02).
Added job_status_transition table (7 allowed moves) and trg_job_requirement_guard (job_requirement_guard()); published_at is now strictly write-once.
closed (4) and filled (5) jobs could be reopened by updating job_status_id = 2, and filled could be set manually while positions remained unfilled.
job_status_transition has no outgoing edges from closed or filled; job_requirement_guard() rejects filled unless positions_filled = positions_total.
No database entry point allowed Talentra staff to verify or reject an organisation (FR-ORG-06); only the schema owner could update verification_status_id.

Added SECURITY DEFINER function organisation_set_verification(org_id, status_code, note) restricted to staff (organisation_verify), enforcing pending -> verified/rejected and rejected -> pending, updating verified_at and tax IDs, and writing an audit_event.
user_device.revoked_at existed in DDL, but v2_app had no UPDATE grant or entry point to revoke a device (FR-IAM-06), and revoked_at was not write-once.

Added auth_revoke_device(device_id) (owner or staff), which sets revoked_at, ends all active sessions on the device, and logs user_device.revoked; added trg_user_device_guard so revoked_at is write-once.
app_user.account_status_id had no transition guard or entry point for suspend/reactivate/deactivate (FR-IAM-04/06).
Added trg_app_user_status_guard (erased is final) and user_set_account_status(user_id, status_code) (staff for suspended, owner/staff for deactivated/active, ending active sessions and auditing).
subscription_guard() blocked extending ends_on or altering limits, but allowed cancelled_at to be reset from a timestamp back to NULL.
Updated subscription_guard() so cancelled_at is write-once (OLD.cancelled_at IS NOT NULL AND NEW.cancelled_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.cancelled_at raises check_violation).

notification_record_result() accepted any status code without checking current status, allowing delivered (3) -> sent (2) or queued (1).
Updated notification_record_result() to validate (OLD.status, NEW.status) against ((1,2),(1,3),(1,4),(2,3),(2,4)), making delivered, failed, and suppressed final.

FOR UPDATE` row locks (`wallet` row for credits, `organisation` row for seats, `app_user` row for devices, `job_requirement` row for positions) inside single-writer functions/triggers + cached counters (`balance_credits`, `positions_filled`) verified by `CHECK` constraints.

• **Decision & Rationale:** Chosen: **Design B**. Under `READ COMMITTED`, two concurrent transactions do not see each other's uncommitted inserts, so a trigger counting rows without a parent lock allows both to pass (write skew). `SERIALIZABLE` fixes this by aborting racing transactions with `40001 serialization_failure`, forcing application retry loops on every hot wallet or job. Design B serialises only the contenders for the *same* wallet/org/user/job in a deterministic queue (`t04_concurrency.sql` proves 8 parallel debits on 3 credits → 3 succeed, 5 cleanly refused with `insufficient credits`, 0 serialization aborts).

Every cross-table policy, calculation, limit, state rule, and constraint is consolidated with a unique ID, owner, enforcement point (**0 gaps**), and verified test:
Every table uses an integer surrogate key id; foreign keys and check constraints are enforced by the database.

Candidates register themselves (or via staff at a placement drive); recruiters/employers cannot register candidates. Sign-up creates user, credential, candidate role, profile, and mandatory terms + privacy consents in one transaction.

A candidate profile is visible to recruiters only when deleted_at IS NULL, profile_visibility_id <> 3 (not hidden), and the candidate currently grants profile_visible_to_recruiters consent (purpose 3).

When a candidate blocks an organisation or user, the blocked party immediately loses visibility of the candidate profile, their applications, and their contact details (even if previously downloaded), and never sees the block row.
RLS on candidate_profile, application, candidate_block + candidate_contact()
Permissions derive strictly from user_access_role -> access_role_permission, and only users with account_status_id = 1 (active) hold any permission.
Consent is an append-only history per user and purpose with policy_version; the latest record (consent_current) governs processing.

Active sessions per user cannot exceed the device limit (3 for candidates; subscription.max_devices_per_user for org members, or 1 without an active subscription). Expired sessions are closed first; revoked devices and over-limit logins are refused and audited.
auth_open_session() with FOR UPDATE lock on app_user + auth_revoke_device()
After 5 consecutive failed password checks, the credential is locked for 15 minutes (locked_until), audited, and refused by auth_open_session(); a successful login resets the counter.

An organisation has at most subscription.max_seats current members (valid_to IS NULL) under its active subscription (1 without one). A user belongs to at most one organisation at any point in time, and closed memberships (valid_to) are write-once.

Tax identifiers (GSTIN, PAN, CIN, VAT, EIN) are validated for format, tokenised via pii_hmac() + identifier_last4, and never stored in clear. Staff verify or reject organisations via organisation_set_verification(), recording verified_at and an audit event.

Publishing a job (draft -> open) sets published_at (write-once) and debits 5 credits from the organisation wallet exactly once (idempotency_key = job_post:<id>). Published jobs never return to draft; closed and filled are final.

Each application moving to joined increments job_requirement.positions_filled under a job row lock; when positions_filled = positions_total, job_status_id automatically becomes filled (5); joins beyond positions_total are refused.

A candidate can apply at most once per job, only while the job is open (2), not deleted, and on or before closes_on, starting in status applied (1). Attached resumes must belong to the candidate; answers must belong to questions of that job.
Applications move only along the 12 edges in application_status_transition; joined, rejected, and withdrawn are final.
A candidate may only transition their own application to withdrawn (7); all forward and rejection moves require an unblocked member of the hiring organisation with application_manage permission.
Every application status change is recorded in application_status_history (append-only) with from_status_id, to_status_id, changed_at, and created_by.

A sold subscription is an immutable licence snapshot (max_seats, max_devices_per_user, starts_on, plan_id cannot change; ends_on cannot be extended; cancelled_at is write-once); subscription periods of one organisation never overlap.

Every organisation has exactly one wallet. wallet.balance_credits equals SUM(wallet_ledger_entry.credits) and is never negative. Ledger entries are append-only; corrections are reversal entries (ledger_entry_type_id = 6) pointing once at the original entry.
trg_organisation_ensure_wallet, wallet_post() with wallet row lock, forbid_change(), ck_wallet_balance_not_negative

Payment webhooks (billing_apply_payment_event) are idempotent on gateway_event_ref, verify event.amount = order.amount, advance payment_order strictly forward (created -> authorised -> captured -> refunded or -> failed), issue a sequential GST invoice (18% tax split) on capture, and reverse granted credits on refund.

Downloading a candidate profile (billing_download_profile) costs 1 credit and grants the organisation 30 days of access to candidate_contact(). Repeat downloads within 30 days are free and return the existing download. Every download and contact reveal is audited.

Notifications are written in the same transaction as the business event (dedupe_key prevents duplicates), honour notification_preference opt-outs and consent_current (except category 3 account_security), never contain PII in payload, and move only queued -> sent -> delivered/failed with exponential backoff up to 5 attempts.

Every sensitive action writes an append-only audit_event via audit_log() (actor taken from app.user_id, never forged by the caller); row-change triggers log changed column names, never personal values.

Right to erasure (candidate_erase) deletes education, experience, skills, languages, job alerts, resumes (queuing object-storage deletion), and credentials; blanks name, headline, summary, city, salary, email, phone, application_answer.answer_text, and user_device.device_label; ends sessions; revokes devices; and retains applications, downloads, and ledgers anonymised.

Organisation parent hierarchy (parent_organisation_id) must remain a strict tree (no self-parenting or cycles), and a recruiter sees and acts only on their own organisation's jobs, applications, and funnel.
Consultant-sourced applications (application_source_id = 3) are permitted only on job requirements where is_open_to_consultants = true.
All UI strings resolve via ui_text(ui_label_id, language_id) with automatic fallback to English (language_id = 1); user-authored text is stored once in UTF-8 with its language tag.

Scheduled retention and maintenance jobs keep high-volume tables bounded: audit_event partitions created monthly and dropped after 7 years; inactive profiles erased after 3 years; ended sessions purged after 1 year; final notifications after 180 days; system errors after 90 days; agg_hiring_funnel_monthly refreshed hourly CONCURRENTLY.

Probable duplicate candidates (same phone_e164 and lower(full_name)), profiles missing current_city_id, experience mismatches, over-seat lapsed orgs, unverified org open jobs, and 90-day stale is_open_to_work profiles are continuously detected by data-quality queries (F-01..F-06).

Reference and configuration tables (language, ui_label, ui_translation, currency, country, state, city, skill, access_role_permission, application_status_transition, job_status_transition, and the 23 lookup tables) omit created_by / updated_by.

Rule Group 2 & 4 (Primary Key & Audit Columns on Logs)
audit_event has composite PK (id, occurred_at) and both audit_event and system_error omit created_at/by, updated_at/by.

PostgreSQL declarative partitioning requires the partition key (occurred_at) in the primary key. Log tables record occurred_at and actor_app_user_id / app_user_id natively and are append-only, so updated_at/by would be redundant.

Role-qualified foreign keys (parent_organisation_id, blocked_organisation_id, blocked_app_user_id, sourced_by_app_user_id, actor_app_user_id, from_status_id, to_status_id, renewed_from_subscription_id, reverses_ledger_entry_id) prepend the role to <table>_id.
Disambiguates self-references and tables with multiple foreign keys to the same parent while still ending in _id (verified by t01_standards.sql L44-49).
Foreign keys pointing to static reference/lookup tables and created_by / updated_by audit columns do not carry dedicated B-tree indexes.

Reference/lookup rows and users with history are RESTRICT-protected and never hard-deleted, so PostgreSQL never scans child tables for cascading deletes on those columns, saving ~35% index storage overhead. Every FK to a business table is indexed (t01_standards.sql L53-59).

decisions: B03 is data requirements and B04 is conceptual modelling
Map B03 sections to4/6/12/13/14/22; B04 to9; preserve D3 lifecycle numbering
Reported G3 victory versus open interview
B overview says passed; gate tracker says author interview pending
Keep G3 open for the hybrid. Do not copy a source-reported gate into a hybrid approval
B assigns D8=4 while interview is pending
Set hybrid human understanding to0 until actual interview evidence exists
B reports PostgreSQL passes but attached workbook contains no DDL repository or raw run logs
Retain as source-reported evidence; it does not verify the A/hybrid schema
B overview mentions PostgreSQL18; physical baseline says PostgreSQL16
Keep A PostgreSQL18 design target. Resolve B runtime version from missing run logs before transferring evidence
293 of462 B-v2 definition/example rows use an em-dash definition
Use meaningful A definitions and available B-v1 descriptions; never count dash text as a complete definition
A has120 physical tables; B has73 including25 lookup tables
Map concepts and domains. Do not sum120+73 or rank model quality by table count
A wallet ledger uses monetary amounts/currency; B uses whole-number product credits
Model credit account/ledger separately as proposed design; never copy credit counts into money columns
B:wallet and wallet_ledger_entry; A wallet definitions
B hard-codes18% tax,5 credits per posting,1 credit per download and30-day access
Retain as proposed configurable policy. Require product/finance/privacy owner confirmation
A baseline inactivity proposal24months; B3years; audit7years
Keep competing policy proposals visible; no automatic legal-policy approval or arithmetic average
B reports5.3ms search at dev10k; source docket requires measured laptop1m profiles
Preserve reported number with dataset qualifier. Keep laptop/full-scale tests pending
B uses one table per vocabulary; A uses reference_domain/value bindings
Keep A domain-scoped lookup strategy; map B vocabulary concepts without duplicating physical enum tables
B treats subscription as licence; A separates licence limits from periods
Retain A licence+period model and bring B immutable sold-plan snapshot policy into the design register
B places intent, delivery and queue metadata on notification
Preserve A separation across notification, notification_delivery, outbox_event and delivery_attempt
B candidate full_name duplicates A app_user.person_name concept
Keep one canonical identity name; map candidate display to owning user rather than adding another authoritative name
B allows staff registration at placement drives
Retain self-registration/no recruiter registration. Staff-assisted exception remains an explicit owner decision
User identifies A as GPT; B model might be Claude/Muse/other but is not recorded
Record A=GPT per user, B=unknown. Report cross-author artifact comparison, not confirmed named-model consensus
Hybrid adds workbook design fields but has not executed a physical migration
Existing120-table A baseline stays the executed portable-design scope; proposed hybrid fields do not inherit its passes
Only A has completed integration/source-mapping artifacts at canonical step22
Retain A contracts. B integration-boundary rows supplement ownership; no second field-level provider contract exists
B reports275=28BR+247DR; the supplied rows have a smaller explicit catalogue
Report observed explicit rows separately from source-reported aggregate. Do not invent absent rules
